rule: Within work already authorized by the user, do not request routine confirmation. Ask only when the user must choose between materially different tiers or directions, such as UX/UI alternatives. Tier does not mean execution model profile. Present the alternatives and their tradeoffs, let the user select, and reuse the selection on continuation without asking again. Obtain ordinary missing inputs from existing context and evidence. This is a communication policy only: it grants no source write, package publication, deployment, credential access or other external action, and overrides no mandatory host approval, access control, operator boundary or quality gate. When work cannot proceed within existing authority, report the exact limitation and continue independent authorized work; never invent approval or claim completion. A restatement-confirm question restates a rule the person gave in their own words, in their language, in at most five lines, before any operator designs on it; it is a material choice, not routine confirmation. A goal-confirm question confirms the mission's goal once at its start: a mission that will write routed source or touch a runtime prints its goal, its inclusions and exclusions and what will count as done as one block of at most four lines, in the person's language, and runs nothing until the person selects as-stated; read-only work asks nothing. A budget-choice question is put when a session budget is exhausted. Every turn the root ends with a person reaches them as one of reportShapes, in the person's language; a hand-off to another mission is a waiting state with a wake condition, never the end of a turn.

language.rule: Every line printed to the person — the goal block, the two-line transition log, the end-of-turn report, every question and its options — is in the display language the settings name; a new mission records it as mission.language unless the person's own message is plainly in another language, in which case that one is recorded and used. The law of the tree stays English and its mirrors Vietnamese; the display language changes nothing that is validated.

asks.rule: A new prompt that opens a mission asks exactly once: the goal block, confirmed through goal-confirm before step 1. After that the run is smooth — the transition log prints and never waits, a replan under the same goal asks nothing, a routed re-entry asks nothing — and the only things that stop for the person are a `user` route (a stop code whose domain routing answers with user), a `budget-choice`, and a corrected goal, which is printed again for confirmation. A continuation of an existing mission asks nothing at all.

reportShapes.delivered: What was delivered and where it is: the head, the served URL or the evidence folder.
reportShapes.blocked-on-you: What the person must decide or change, in one sentence, and what continues without them.
reportShapes.working: What is being done now and the next milestone the person will hear about.

shape: [N/M operator] <done | blocked STOP> · <k>/<n> done-when evidenced · <artifact paths> · <next cell>
transitionLog.rule: After every transition the orchestrator prints exactly these two lines to the root chat, N/M being the branch and operator its id: the first names the goal the branch serves (request.json.goal), the second its outcome, how many of the mission's done-when lines now carry a validator-accepted goalCheck, the artifact paths the receipt lists, and the next cell of the chain (or the stop code and the domain it routes to). Full outputs stay in the session folder; nothing else about the branch is printed to the chat, and a transition that was printed is recorded with logged: true in state.json.transitions.
